googlePolicy.framerError: quic_connection.cc:823-831 drops errors while disconnected or while the last packet has not been decrypted; an authenticated framer error closes the connection.
googlePolicy.decryptFailure: quic_framer.cc:1906-1927 reports an undecryptable packet before raising QUIC_DECRYPTION_FAILURE; the connection policy above does not close for that ordinary unauthenticated failure.
googlePolicy.integrityLimitException: quic_connection.cc:2744-2789 counts authentication failures when a decryption key exists and closes at the AEAD integrity limit. Ordinary drop policy does not imply unlimited authentication failures.

cloudflarePolicy.ffi: ffi.rs:875-888 converts Connection::recv Ok(bytes) directly to bytes and Err(error) through Error::to_c; Done=-1 and BufferTooShort=-2 in error.rs:205-209.
cloudflarePolicy.ordinaryMalformedOrDecryptFailure: lib.rs:3022-3031 and 3351-3360 route header parsing and payload decryption failures through drop_pkt_on_err. Lines9463-9494 explicitly limit that mapper to errors before authentication. On a client it maps these failures to Done even when recv_count is zero.
cloudflarePolicy.doneIsConsumed: lib.rs:2910-2937 consumes recv_single Done as the remaining datagram length; it first checks for stateless reset, which can mark the connection closed. Thus an ordinary discarded malformed/decrypt-failed packet returns a nonnegative consumed length from public recv.
cloudflarePolicy.duplicate: lib.rs:3362-3365 returns Done for an already received packet number; the same consumed/drop rule applies.
cloudflarePolicy.fatal: lib.rs:2931-2937 closes with the transport wire error before returning any other recv_single error. Authenticated protocol errors must not be blanket-ignored by a wrapper.
cloudflarePolicy.zeroLengthException: lib.rs:2862-2864 returns BufferTooShort before close for an empty buffer. Reachability through the Dart UDP layer was not investigated; this audit does not establish a production mismatch.
cloudflarePolicy.closingVersusClosed: lib.rs:7623-7666 requires normal recv/send/timeout handling until is_closed after close, except immediate close if no packet was successfully processed. Lines7890-7924 distinguish terminal is_closed from local_error, whose presence neither implies closed nor proves transmission to the peer.
cloudflarePolicy.exampleLimit: client.c:134-149 continues after a negative recv return and later checks is_closed. That event-loop strategy permits shutdown processing; it does not prove the core leaves a negative-error connection usable for HTTP requests.

conclusion.recommendation: Preserve the current Dart negative-below-Done error handling for this scope. Do not blanket-ignore negative recv results based on the C example. The core already discards ordinary unauthenticated bad packets. No production repair is justified by this source audit.
limits: This compares public library control flow, not independently executed original Spotify behavior or actual outgoing bytes.
No error-return frequency, empty-datagram reachability, packet-capture equality or end-to-end shutdown equivalence is claimed.
No changes to pacing, connection shutdown/draining, error classification, Dart production code or tests are included.
